subject: Billing alignment and conditional uplift agreement
messages:
From: Sarah Keller <sarah.keller@novacentral.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@novacentral.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Q3 renewal — capacity planning and pricing ask

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. NovaCentral's Q3 renewal window is coming up (contract ends 2027-07-31) and procurement asked me to lock in pricing certainty while we scope a likely 35-50% uptick in inference usage over the next 6–9 months.

High-level asks from our side:
- Can Redwood hold our current effective rate for at least 3 months post-renewal while we ramp?
- Can you provide a short-term bridging credit for usage above our committed tier during the first 60 days of any uplift?
- We prefer invoices on net60 (internal requirement) and a PO-based workflow.

Attached is last quarter's usage export (usage_march2027.csv) and a draft PO template. Let me know the simplest path to a commercial amendment or short-term addendum.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Sarah Keller
Head of Procurement, NovaCentral
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: usage_march2027.csv (CSV, 92KB)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Keller <sarah.keller@novacentral.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 renewal — capacity planning and pricing ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the details and the export. I reviewed the CSV quickly and see the March burst patterns you called out. Short answer: we can get you the certainty you want while preserving Redwood's ability to fairly price sustained uplift.

Proposed operational approach (high level):
1) 90-day price hold at your current effective blended rate for baseline + a 25% uplift buffer.
2) For incremental usage above that buffer during the first 60 days after uplift, we apply a bridging credit of 40% off list (i.e., discount on overage tokens) to smooth the transition.
3) If the uplift sustains beyond the initial 90 days, we convert the uplift into a staged contractual uplift (tiered commit) with a 6-month review cadence.
4) We can route invoices Net60 on renewals where procurement requires it; finance will need the PO reference and a signed amendment.

I copied Ben (account lead) to draft a short term-sheet and Marissa for commercial approval. Ben — can you translate this into a term sheet with explicit numbers and attach an editable PDF? Also please include a DocuSign-ready version.

Sarah — quick Q: is the Net60 requirement absolute or negotiable to Net45 if needed to avoid delaying provisioning?

Best,
Irene
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
+1 510-555-0246
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Q3 renewal — capacity planning and pricing ask

Sarah / Irene — thanks. Attached is a concise term sheet that formalizes Irene's approach and adds line-item examples. Key points captured:

- Term: 12-month renewal starting 2027-08-01 with an initial 90-day price hold at current blended effective rate for baseline + 25% uplift buffer.
- Bridging credit: 40% off list on overage tokens for first 60 days where usage > buffer; credit applied as a line-item on next invoice (example included).
- Staged uplift: if uplift >= 30% in any consecutive 60-day window after the 90-day hold, parties convert uplift to a committed tier for the remainder of the contract at an agreed step-up rate (example matrix in attachment).
- Invoice terms: Net60 accepted for this amendment provided PO# is included and DocuSign is completed within 7 business days of the commercial sign.
- CapEx vs OpEx: no changes (we'll keep billing as OpEx).

Action items listed in the term sheet:
1) NovaCentral signs the short amendment (DocuSign link below).
2) Redwood generates amended order form and issues first invoice with PO reference on Net60.
3) Finance applies bridging credits as described if overage conditions are met.

Attachments: TermSheet_Nova_20270415.pdf (PDF, stub)
DocuSign: https://docusign.example/sign/ABCD-1234
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/DEAL-2027-0197

If you're good with the economics I can send the DocuSign package today. Also flagging Marissa for quick commercial approval — Marissa, does the 40% credit for the first 60 days look reasonable as a smoothing concession?

Thanks,
Ben Carter

1) Can the bridging credit be applied as an invoice credit within the same billing cycle rather than a subsequent invoice? That's important for our cash reconciliation.
2) The Net60 requirement is non-negotiable for us; can Redwood accept Net60 and confirm provisioning won't be delayed if our procurement cycle pushes sign to day +5?

We attached the PO template populated with our PO number and internal approver (PO_78934.pdf). If both items above are OK, we can route this through DocuSign today.
